public_rationale: The adverse-judgment component has evidence: the Munich court largely upheld GEMA's copyright claims against OpenAI. The forecast also requires that such a loss cause a broad reckoning in model use across industries. The reviewed evidence does not establish that consequence. The complete forecast remains unresolved; a partial match does not justify support, and an unspecified future consequence has not failed merely because it remains unverified.
limitations: The official source is a court summary, not the complete judgment.
The judgment was not final when announced.
The claimed downstream effect is broad and has no deadline.

our_interpretation: The forecast requires both an adverse copyright judgment against a generative AI company of the kind discussed and substantial consequences for model use across adopting industries.
Losing a lawsuit includes an adverse merits judgment; an allegation or settlement alone is insufficient.
A reckoning means broad restrictions, withdrawals or substantial restructuring of model use, not merely legal commentary or a single licensing agreement.
The judgment must cause the cross-industry changes.
criteria.support_condition: An adverse copyright judgment is followed by documented, substantial changes in AI model use across adopting industries caused by that judgment.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Decisive evidence makes the predicted sequence impossible. A company winning another case or the passage of time alone cannot disprove an eventual sequence.
